Let me analyze this OIML certificate.

Certificate number: R076/2006-A-CH1-2019.05 Rev. 6
Scheme: A
Member state: Switzerland
Date issued: 2024-10-17
OIML issuer ID: CH1

Issuing authority: Federal Institute of Metrology METAS, Conformity Evaluation Body METAS-Cert, Lindenweg 50, 3003 Bern-Wabern, Switzerland. Person responsible: Gulian Couvreur, Head of METAS-Cert. Phone +41 58 387 01 11, www.metas.ch. OIML issuer ID: CH1.

Applicant: Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG, Otto-Brenner-Strasse 20, 37079 Göttingen, Germany.

Manufacturer: Sartorius Scientific Instruments (Beijing) Co., Limited, Yu An Road No. 33, Zone B, Tianzhu Airport Industrialzone, Shunyi District, 101 300 Beijing, PR China.

Certified type: Precision balances BC-E and BC-A Line. Types: BC-EI, BC-EJ, BC-AI, BC-AJ.

Recommendation: R 76-1, edition 2006. So canonical id "R76", edition 2006... Wait — R76-1 is part 1 of R76. The schema says id canonical e.g. "R60". Edition int — 2006. Hmm, for R76 the edition is 2006. Amendment: null. Scheme: A. Accuracy classes: ["II"].

Metrological characteristics table:

- Type: BC-EI, BC-AI | BC-EJ, BC-AJ (two column groups)
- Accuracy class: ( II ) both
- Max: 5 000 g … 8 200 g both
- e: 1 g both
- d: 0.1 g - 1 g both
- n: ≤ 8 200 both
- Tare-balancing range: until 100% of Max
- Temperature range: +10 °C / +30 °C
- Nominal capacity of the load receptor: 9 840 g
- Initial zero setting + dead load 1): ≤ 4 840 g
- Maximum weighing pan size: 180 mm x 180 mm (BC-EI, BC-AI) | Ø 180 mm (BC-EJ, BC-AJ)

So this is a family of 4 models. The varying attribute is "maximum_weighing_pan_size". Actually the two columns are BC-EI, BC-AI vs BC-EJ, BC-AJ. So models: BC-EI, BC-EJ, BC-AI, BC-AJ. The pan size differs by column: rectangular models (EI, AI) 180mm x 180mm; round models (EJ, AJ) Ø 180 mm.

Pan size isn't numeric; it's a dimension description. I could record model_level with value as string "180 mm x 180 mm" vs "Ø 180 mm". Hmm, but the strict structured value requires object with value/unit. Value could be string "180 mm x 180 mm", unit null. Or I could split into pan_size_width/length... That's noisy. Let me record:

model_level:
- maximum_capacity: values per model, 5000-8200 range {min: 5000, max: 8200} g
- verification_scale_interval_e: 1 g per model
- actual_scale_interval_d: {min: 0.1, max: 1} g per model
- max_number_of_scale_intervals_n: {min: null, max: 8200} per model
- maximum_weighing_pan_size: string per model

type_level:
- accuracy_class: "II"
- tare_balancing_range: "100% of Max" → value 100, unit "%", reference Max. Could be {value: 100, unit_symbol: "%"} plus maybe a note. Let me keep as value: "100% of Max"? The rule says formulas/symbols keep as string. "until 100% of Max" — I could do value: 100, unit "%", and maybe add a note. Simpler: value: "100% of Max". Hmm. Rules say separate numeric from unit. "until 100% of Max" → value: {min: null, max: 100}? "until 100%" means ≤100%. I'd do value: {min: null, max: 100}, unit_symbol: "%", and perhaps add "reference": Max. But schema for characteristic value object shape is {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}. No reference field shown, but the R60 example had safe_overload_reference as separate characteristic. I could add attribute "tare_balancing_range_reference": {"value": "Max"}. Maybe simpler: one attribute tare_balancing_range with value {min: null, max: 100} and unit "%" — that's clean. Since tare range of "until 100% of Max" relative to Max. I'll do that.

- temperature_range: +10/+30 °C → {min: 10, max: 30} °C
- nominal_capacity_of_load_receptor: 9840 g
- initial_zero_setting_plus_dead_load: ≤4840 g, footnote "1)"
- maximum_weighing_pan_size: model_level since it varies.

Footnote 1) — the markdown shows superscript 1) on "Initial zero setting + dead load 1)" but there's no footnote definition text visible in the markdown. Hmm. Rule 7 says extract footnote definitions; if not present, don't fabricate. But the marker is referenced. I should include footnote_markers: ["1)"] on the value but no footnotes[] entry since no definition text found. Actually maybe I should include footnote marker only. The footnotes array only if definitions exist. There's no definition text in the doc. So footnotes[] omitted or empty. I'll omit.

Models: BC-EI, BC-EJ, BC-AI, BC-AJ. The table groups BC-EI, BC-AI in one column and BC-EJ, BC-AJ in another. The distinguishing attribute: pan size — rectangular vs round (EI/AI = rectangular 180x180, EJ/AJ = round Ø180). "E" vs "A" likely refers to BC-E line vs BC-A line.

Model family:
- family_name: "Precision balances BC-E and BC-A Line" — that's the certified type description; could serve as family name. I'll set family_name: "BC-E and BC-A Line".
- models: BC-EI, BC-EJ, BC-AI, BC-AJ.

Since Max, e, d, n are identical for all models, they could be type_level. But the table presents them per column; they're identical though. I'll put them in type_level (single value) and only pan size in model_level. Actually, the schema's model_level is for varying attributes. Pan size varies. Everything else identical → type_level.

But maybe to be safe and traceable, put the per-model attributes in model_level? The instructions: "Detect this and put varying attributes in model_level, NOT type_level." Only pan size varies. So model_level: maximum_weighing_pan_size.

Wait — the model_level values entries: {model, value, footnote_markers[]}. Value shape is structured {value, unit_symbol, ...}? Looking at R137 example: {"model": "G1.6", "value": 2.5} — no unit_symbol inside values; the unit is at the attribute level (unit_symbol: "m³/h"). So model_level entry: {attribute, unit_symbol, values: [{model, value}]}. OK.

For pan size: attribute "maximum_weighing_pan_size", unit_symbol null, values: [{model: "BC-EI", value: "180 mm x 180 mm"}, {model: "BC-AI", value: "180 mm x 180 mm"}, {model: "BC-EJ", value: "Ø 180 mm"}, {model: "BC-AJ", value: "Ø 180 mm"}].

Hmm but the strict rule says every characteristic value MUST be an object with value/unit_symbol. For model_level, the example shows values as plain {model, value}. I'll follow the example format. But to be safe, maybe make values structured: {"model": "BC-EI", "value": {"value": "180 mm x 180 mm", "unit_symbol": null, ...}}? The example in rule 4 shows {"model": "G1.6", "value": 2.5} — plain value. I'll follow that.

Actually, could also represent pan size numerically: width 180 mm, length 180 mm, diameter 180 mm. Alternative: config-level axis "pan_shape". Simpler to keep strings.

Test reports:
- 6030-01226-06, date 2024-10-17, pages 12, role type_evaluation_report.
Documentation file:
- R076_2006-A-CH1-2019.05_Rev_06_LERD_V01, date 2024-10-17, pages 6, role documentation_file.

Revision history:
- 00, 2019-09-24, First issue
- 01, 2020-09-24, Extension with the types BC-AI, BC-AJ
- 02, 2020-11-03, Editorial changes
- 03, 2021-04-15, Rebranding, new design

- 06, 2024-10-17, Change of the socket for power supply from SMD (Surface Mounted Device) to THT (Through Hole Technology). Therefore, modification of the mainboard has been conducted.

Revision as string: "00" etc.

Certificate number: "R076/2006-A-CH1-2019.05" with revision 6. The number given: "No R076/2006-A-CH1-2019.05 Rev. 6". So number: "R076/2006-A-CH1-2019.05", revision "6". Page_total: 3. Project_number: maybe "6030-01226-06"? That's the test report number, not project. I won't set project_number. Actually the METAS project number could be 6030-01226; but it's listed as the type evaluation report number. Leave out.

Certificate category: "Precision balance" — category examples include "Load cell", "Indicator"... I'll use "Precision balance".

Module designation: not applicable / not mentioned → null or omit. I'll set "Not applicable"? Only if mentioned. Omit — actually schema says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. I'll set null or omit. I'll omit it to avoid fabrication. Hmm, the schema lists it as a field; setting null is fine.

Date issued: 2024-10-17 (from "3003 Bern-Wabern, 2024-10-17").

OIML issuer ID: CH1 ("The OIML Issuing Authority CH1").

Recommendation: R 76-1, edition 2006. Canonical id: "R76". Some might say "R76-1" since part 1. The schema example: id "R60" not "OIML R 60". For R76-1, the certificate is for part 1 (metrological and technical requirements). I think "R76" is canonical; the "-1" is the part. Hmm. I'll use "R76" and maybe include part in... there's no part field. Accuracy classes: ["II"]. Scheme: "A".

Phone: +41 58 387 01 11. Website: www.metas.ch.

Person responsible: Gulian Couvreur. Person title: "Head of METAS-Cert" (page 1) / page 3 says "Head of sector METAS-Cert". I'll use "Head of METAS-Cert".

Address lines: ["Lindenweg 50", "3003 Bern-Wabern", "Switzerland"] or one line "Lindenweg 50, 3003 Bern-Wabern, Switzerland". I'll split.

Now characteristics:

type_level:
- accuracy_class: {"value": "II", "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null, "footnote_markers": []}
- maximum_capacity: {"value": {"min": 5000, "max": 8200}, "unit_symbol": "g", ...}
- verification_scale_interval_e: 1 g
- actual_scale_interval_d: {min: 0.1, max: 1} g
- max_number_of_scale_intervals_n: {min: null, max: 8200} (dimensionless)
- tare_balancing_range: {min: null, max: 100}, "%"
- temperature_range: {min: 10, max: 30}, "°C"
- nominal_capacity_of_load_receptor: 9840 g
- initial_zero_setting_plus_dead_load: {min: null, max: 4840}, "g", footnote ["1)"]

model_level:
- maximum_weighing_pan_size with 4 model entries.

Canonical labels: "Max" → maximum_capacity. "e" → verification_scale_interval (scale interval). "d" → actual_scale_interval. "n" → number_of_scale_intervals. I'll use maximum_capacity, verification_scale_interval_e? The rule examples: `Max. number of load cell intervals nLC` → `max_load_cell_intervals_nlc`. So keep the symbol suffix. I'll use:
- maximum_capacity (Max)
- scale_interval_e → "verification_scale_interval" or "scale_interval_e". I'll use "scale_interval_e".
- scale_interval_d → "actual_scale_interval_d". Hmm consistency: I'll use "scale_interval_e" and "scale_interval_d".
- number_of_scale_intervals_n.
- tare_balancing_range
- temperature_range
- nominal_capacity_of_load_receptor
- initial_zero_setting_plus_dead_load
- maximum_weighing_pan_size

Footnote markers: format "1)" per example in schema ("footnote_markers": ["1)"]).

Matrix tables: the metrological characteristics table fits into characteristics; no need for matrix_tables. But maybe include the table? The schema says matrix_tables for multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. The char table is captured. I'll skip matrix_tables.

Model family models: include label/attributes? Each model: model_id "BC-EI", label maybe "BC-EI (BC-E Line, rectangular pan 180 mm × 180 mm)". Keep simple: model_id and maybe attributes for line: {"line": "BC-E", "pan_shape": "rectangular"}. That could be helpful but risks fabrication. "BC-E and BC-A Line" — EI/EJ are E line, AI/AJ are A line. That's an inference but reasonable from naming and revision 01 "Extension with the types BC-AI, BC-AJ". I'll include attributes {"line": "BC-E"} etc. Light inference, acceptable. Actually rule 8 says don't fabricate. The line assignment is directly derivable from the type names and family name. I'll include it.

Pan size per model: BC-EI and BC-AI → "180 mm x 180 mm"; BC-EJ and BC-AJ → "Ø 180 mm".
